He was carrying a plastic bag. Reaching inside, he pulled out a baseball glove.
"Are you sure you want to risk losing your autographed glove?" Cole asked. "It's really cool. Plus your parents will be mad if you lose it."
"I won't lose it," Henry said. "We'll be hiding and watching it, remember?"

That was his plan. The baseball glove had been autographed by several famous baseball players. Anyone could see it was worth a lot of money. Henry was planning to put the glove in the barn aisle where everyone would notice it. Then he and Cole would hide out and see if anyone tried to take it. With luck, they'd catch the thief before Maggie's riding lesson started!
"If Jill is stealing because she needs money, she'll definitely grab this glove," Cole said.

"If Zach's the thief, he might take it too," Henry said. "He loves baseball. And we don't know what Eleanor's motive might be. Maybe she needs money too. My aunt and uncle keep saying that riding is an expensive sport."
He set his glove down. Then he and Cole hid in an empty stall nearby.
It wasn't long before they heard footsteps. Henry peeked out and saw Zach coming down the aisle.
"Hey, what's that?" Zach muttered. He stopped and picked up the glove. "Whoa, cool!" he said. "Guess someone will come back to look for this."
He dropped the glove where he'd found it. Then he kept walking.
"Zach didn't take the bait!" Cole whispered. "I guess he's innocent."
Henry nodded. "Shh! Here comes Eleanor."
Eleanor hurried down the aisle. "Spot? Spot, where are you?" she called.
She was so busy calling her dog that she almost tripped over the glove before she saw it.
Then she stopped, looking confused. She leaned down for a better look at the glove. Finally she shrugged and hurried off, still calling Spot.
"Eleanor didn't take it either," Cole whispered.
Henry just nodded. He'd heard the sound of Jill's wheelbarrow rolling toward them.
The older girl saw the glove right away. She stopped her wheelbarrow. Then she hurried over, grabbed the glove, and took off down the aisle!
Henry gasped. "Jill took the baseball glove!" he said. "She must be the barn thief!"
"Let's get your glove back before she hides it somewhere," Cole said.
Both boys jumped out of their hiding place. Jill had already disappeared around the corner. But they could hear her calling Maggie's name.
"That's weird," said Henry. "Why is she yelling for Maggie?"
He ran toward Big Spot's stall with Cole right behind him. They got there just in time to see Jill handing Henry's baseball glove to Maggie.
"I found this lying on the floor," Jill said with a frown. "I assume it belongs to your cousin or his friend. You'd better tell them that this is a barn, not a baseball field."
"You can tell them yourself," Maggie said. "They're right behind you."
"Oh!" Jill spun around and saw Henry and Cole. "Does this glove belong to one of you? Because I have enough to do around here without picking up after visitors."
"It's mine," Henry said. "Sorry about that."
"That's okay." Jill shrugged. "Just don't do it again, okay?"
"Oh well," Cole said after she was gone. "That plan didn't work."
Maggie looked worried. "You'd better hurry and figure out a better plan," she said. "It's already time for my lesson to start."

She led Big Spot out of his stall and down the aisle toward the riding ring. "Maybe we should watch the lesson," Cole said. "It doesn't seem like Jill is the thief. Or Zach or Eleanor.That means we need to watch Daisy."

"Okay. I guess it's safe to leave my glove here since nobody seems to want to steal it," Henry said. "But should we take Maggie's stuff with us?" He picked up the bag. "I don't want anything else to get stolen."
Cole sneezed. "No way! Put that down," he said. "Cat hair flies out of it every time you touch it. Maggie must have let her kittens sleep in it."
"Probably." Henry set the bag down. "Aunt Ellen says the kittens get into everything."
"I can tell." Cole pointed to the bag. "Look, isn't that a cat toy?"
"Yes." Henry laughed and grabbed the mouse-shaped toy. "The kittens probably batted it inside, and Maggie didn't notice. I'd better stick it in the bottom of the bag so the barn cat doesn't grab it."
"Yeah." Cole grinned. "That's all we need—another thief!"
Leaving the bag behind, the boys headed outside to watch the lesson. They were halfway to the riding ring when Little Spot ran over to them.
"Hi, Little Spot," Cole said, rubbing the beagle's ears.
Henry was looking at the ring. Ms. Wood was in the center with three riders trotting around her.
"It looks like Daisy isn't here today," Henry said.
"Really?" Cole stopped petting Little Spot and stood up. "That means if she's the thief, nothing will disappear today."
Henry nodded. "Right! That could be why my glove . . ."
He stopped talking in the middle of his sentence. Eleanor had jumped down from her pony and run out the gate. She had almost reached the area where the boys were standing.
"Are you okay?" Henry called to her.
"I'm fine," Eleanor said. "I just need to go inside and get a tissue."
She raced past, heading for the barn. Little Spot barked and ran after his owner.
"That's weird," Cole said. "Couldn't she wait until the end of the lesson to get a tissue? That could be suspicious behavior."
"Maybe," Henry said. "But Eleanor is always complaining about how hard she's working, remember? Maybe she just used the tissue story as an excuse to take a break."
"Oh yeah." Cole shrugged. "You're probably right."
Henry and Cole walked the rest of the way to the ring.
Maggie and Zach were still riding while Ms. Wood watched and gave them tips. A few minutes later, Eleanor came out of the barn. Soon she was back on her pony.
When the lesson ended, Maggie led her pony over to the boys. "Did you solve the mystery yet?" she asked them.
"Not yet," Henry said. "But we noticed Daisy is absent. If she's the thief, nothing will get stolen today."
"Oh! Good point." Maggie nodded. "You just have to figure out a way to prove it."
"Don't worry, we will," said Henry.
"Okay." Maggie didn't look too sure about that. Just then Eleanor led her pony up to them, so The Lemonade Detectives had to stop discussing the case.
They all walked into the barn. Maggie led Spot into his stall, and then turned to put her riding helmet in her bag. As soon as she leaned over, she let out a shriek.
"I can't believe this!" she yelled. "One of my sandals is gone!"
Henry looked over Maggie's shoulder. One of her sandals was in her bag. The other was nowhere in sight.
"The barn thief struck again!" Henry exclaimed. "Cole and I were looking at your bag right before we came outside. Both sandals were definitely in there then."
Cole nodded. "I guess this means Daisy isn't the thief."
"It's another weird theft," Henry said. "Who would steal one sandal?"
Cole grinned. "The same person who would steal one sock!"
"This isn't funny!" Maggie complained. "My parents are going to kill me!"
"Not if we can catch the thief," Henry said. "This could be another clue."
"What do you mean?" Cole asked.
"Daisy didn't steal that sandal," Henry said. "We also know it wasn't Zach."
"We do?" Maggie asked.
"Yes," Cole chimed in. "Zach was in the riding ring when the sandal disappeared, so he couldn't have taken it. But what about Eleanor? She went back into the barn to get a tissue."
"Exactly what I was thinking," Henry replied. "Jill could have done it too. She was inside working the whole time."
"So what are you waiting for?" Maggie asked. "Go question them!"
"Aren't you coming with us?" Cole asked.
"I can't." Maggie stepped toward her pony's stall. "I need to take care of Big Spot first. Ms. Wood is already mad at me about that missing saddle pad, remember?"
Henry was secretly relieved. Sometimes Maggie got too excited when she was questioning people. They'd probably have better luck without her.
"We'll be back soon," he said.
Then he and Cole went to find their suspects. They found Eleanor first. She was taking the saddle off her pony.
"Hi," Henry said. "Are you feeling okay?"
"What do you mean?" Eleanor asked.
"We were worried because you were in the barn for a while," Henry said. "You know, when you went to get a tissue. We thought you might be sick."
Eleanor gave him a funny look. "I'm fine," she said. "I got a tissue, and then I stopped to get Little Spot a drink of water. He was hot and thirsty from running around the barn."
"Oh." Henry tried to think of another question. But he couldn't come up with anything. He looked at Cole, who shrugged.
"Okay," Cole said. "See you later."
They walked away. "That didn't tell us anything," Henry said. "Let's find Jill."
Jill was cleaning a saddle in the tack room. "Hi," Cole said. "Have you been in here the whole time?"
"What do you mean?" Jill sounded grumpy.
Henry thought fast. "We were wondering if you'd seen my baseball glove. I think I lost it again."

That wasn't true. Henry's glove was still sitting near Big Spot's stall. But Henry figured that if Jill had taken Maggie's sandal, she'd probably seen his glove sitting nearby. Maybe she would say something to give herself away.
But Jill just rolled her eyes. "Sorry. I told you before. I don't have time to keep track of your stuff."
Henry sighed. So far their questioning wasn't going very well. Maybe it was time to think of another plan.
He stepped out of the tack room. But he had to stop suddenly as a furry shape raced past him at top speed. Another furry shape was right behind the first one.
"What was that?" Cole peered over Henry's shoulder.
"I think Little Spot is chasing the barn cat," Henry said. "Let's go rescue her!"
They chased the dog and cat down the aisle. The cat stopped at the end and turned to face the dog. Little Spot lunged forward with his mouth open.
"Oh no!" Cole exclaimed. "He's going to bite her!"
But Little Spot didn't bite the cat. He licked her! The cat just sat there as the dog licked her again and again.
Henry laughed at the grumpy expression on the cat's face. "I don't think she likes being licked," he said.
"No," Cole agreed. "But Little Spot is enjoying himself!"
Henry watched the beagle for a moment. "Come on," he said. "I have an idea."
"What?" Cole followed as Henry rushed away.
Henry didn't stop to explain. They didn't have much time to test his new theory. When he reached Big Spot's stall, he stopped. "Give me that cat toy from your bag," he said to Maggie.
"What cat toy?" Maggie stopped brushing the pony, looking confused.
Henry was already digging into her bag. "I'm going to set another trap," he said, pulling out the cat toy.
Cole looked doubtful. "Who would want to steal that thing, other than the barn cat?"
"The same thief who would steal one sock or one sandal." Henry smiled. "I'll explain on the way. We've got to hurry!"
"Are you sure about this?" Maggie whispered.
Henry didn't answer. He, Cole, and Maggie were crouched in an empty stall. They were watching the cat toy, which was lying in the aisle.
"Shh," Henry whispered. "Someone's coming."
Jill came into view. She spotted the cat toy and stopped. She looked up and down the aisle, and then leaned over to pick it up.
Henry held his breath. Was his theory wrong?
Jill straightened up again, dropping the cat toy back on the ground. "I don't get paid enough to pick up after messy riders," she muttered to herself.
Henry let out his breath as she hurried away. So far his plan was going okay.
He heard a bark as Little Spot trotted into sight. The dog paused to sniff the cat toy before lifting his head to look around the barn.
Henry held his breath again. Was the dog going to walk away from the cat toy too?
But Little Spot finally lowered his head, grabbed the toy, and took off.
"Hurry!" Henry exclaimed. "We have to follow him!"
He ran after Little Spot. Maggie and Cole were right behind him.
The dog ran through the barn and out a side door. He crossed a courtyard and ran into another building.
"He's headed for the hay shed!" Maggie said.
Inside the shed, hay bales were stacked halfway to the ceiling. At first Henry couldn't see where Little Spot had gone. Then he heard a muffled bark.
"This way!" Cole rushed around the bales.
They found Little Spot in a narrow space behind the hay. He was wagging his tail and sitting on a dusty saddle pad.
"Big Spot's saddle pad!" Maggie cried. "And look! The rest of my missing stuff is here too!"

She grabbed her charm bracelet and slipped it on, and then picked up the cat toy. Next she dug through the hay until she found her brush, gloves, sock, and sandal. She even found the lost check. It was crumpled and had a few teeth holes in it.
"I'll go tell Ms. Wood we solved the crime," Cole offered, hurrying back out.
Henry spotted something else in the hay. "Look, Spot must have stolen this stuff too."
"That looks like one of Ms. Wood's spare halters," Maggie said. "And here's another grooming brush!"
Soon Ms. Wood arrived, along with Eleanor.

"Little Spot!" Eleanor exclaimed, grabbing her dog and hugging him. "You rotten little thief! I'm really sorry, you guys. He does this at home sometimes, but I never thought he'd do it here. Usually he only steals stuff that smells like cats. For some reason he loves cats!"
Henry grinned. "Yeah, we just figured that out," he said. "I saw him licking the barn cat. That's when I realized why he was mostly stealing from Maggie. All her stuff smells like cats!"
Eleanor gasped. "I didn't know you had cats, Maggie!"
"I have two kittens," Maggie said. "They're really cute."

Ms. Wood picked up the saddle pad. "I owe you an apology, Maggie," she said. "I'm sorry I accused you of losing this. I guess you got some cat hair on it and that's why Spot took it." She noticed the halter. "Sometimes the barn cat knocks down the spare halters and sleeps on them."
Maggie held up the second brush. "And I bet someone used this to brush the cat."
"I'm sorry," Eleanor said. "I promise to watch Little Spot more closely from now on."
"That's okay." Maggie shrugged. "It's just a good thing The Lemonade Detectives were here to solve the case."

"The Lemonade Detectives?" Ms. Wood looked at Henry, Cole, and Maggie. "I've heard about you three! My neighbor hired you when he couldn't remember who'd borrowed his tennis racket. He said you tracked it down within an hour."
Cole nodded. "That was us."
Ms. Wood put a hand in her pocket. "Then I'd better pay your detective fee," she said. "Five dollars, right?"
"You don't have to pay us," Henry said. "Maggie's the one who wanted us to solve this case."

"I insist." Ms. Wood handed him a five-dollar bill. "You found several of my missing things. More importantly you proved that one of my favorite new students isn't careless." She smiled at Maggie. "That's worth at least five dollars, right?"
"Definitely," Maggie agreed. "Henry and Cole saved the day. If they hadn't solved the case, I might have had to stop riding!" She shook her head and smiled. "And all because of a cat-loving dog!"
Little Spot barked and wagged his tail. Everyone laughed.
"Thanks," Henry said, taking the money from Ms. Wood. "I guess that's another case closed for The Lemonade Detectives!"
"I still can't believe Mrs. Smith left her glasses in her bird feeder," Henry said.
"I know." His cousin Maggie laughed. "She's lucky a bird didn't peck them."

"No, she's lucky that The Lemonade Detectives were around to track them down for her," said Henry's friend Cole. The Lemonade Detectives had been in business all summer. They'd solved lots of cases. Some cases were pretty simple, like finding Mrs. Smith's lost glasses. Other cases were trickier. But so far The Lemonade Detectives had solved them all.
"Here come some customers." Henry saw two teenage girls walking toward them. "I wonder whether they want to buy lemonade or hire us to solve a mystery."
"It's a mystery to me!" Cole joked with a grin.
"Not to me," Maggie said, smiling. "Ashley and Jill buy at least one cup of lemonade apiece almost every day!"
Sure enough the older girls ordered two lemonades. While Maggie was pouring their drinks, Ashley took a piece of paper out of her pocket.
"Are you guys busy next Saturday?" She held out the paper. "Because we're having a fundraiser for the Belltown High School soccer team."
"Ugh!" Cole groaned. "Don't talk about school! It's still summer, remember?"
"Only for a few more weeks," Henry said.
Ashley laughed. "I know. That's why we're holding the fundraiser."
Jill nodded. "We're raising money before school starts so we can get new uniforms."
Henry looked at the paper. It said:
BELLTOWN HIGH SCHOOL FUNDRAISER
Enjoy the end of summer with a bike ride through
beautiful Belltown Park
All profits used to support the girls' soccer team
$10 per person, snacks provided
Cole was reading over Henry's shoulder. "Wow. That sounds cool. I love biking on those trails."
"You can keep the flyer," Ashley said. "If you decide to come, just bring your bike, a helmet, and ten dollars." Then she and Jill wandered off with their lemonade.
Cole was still looking at the flyer. "We're going, right?" he said.
"I'd like to do it," Henry said. "It sounds like fun, and it's for a good cause."
"What about the lemonade stand?" Maggie asked.
"We probably won't have many customers that day anyway," Cole pointed out. "Lots of kids will be at the park."
"Maybe you're right," Maggie said. "Besides we made lots of money this week. I guess we can donate some of it to a good cause."
It was the day of the fundraiser. The Lemonade Detectives had just ridden their bikes into Belltown Park.
"Wow. There are tons of people here!" Cole exclaimed.
"It looks like we sign in over there." Maggie pointed to a table draped with Belltown High School's colors, blue and white. Ashley and Jill were sitting behind the table with some of their teammates.
Henry walked over. "Hi. We're here to ride."
"Great!" Jill smiled. "Ten dollars each, please."
Henry and his friends handed over their money. In exchange, Jill handed each of them a ticket.
"Make sure you don't lose those," she said. "Everyone who finishes the ride gets a T-shirt at the end."
"Really?" Maggie looked surprised. "How can you afford that? I thought you were trying to raise money."
Ashley heard her and looked over. "The T-shirts are being donated by Belltown Bikes," she said. "They're our sponsor." She pointed to a sign advertising the local bicycle shop.
Meanwhile Henry heard someone calling his name. It was his friend Nathan.
"Are you guys riding too?" Nathan asked.
"Yeah," Cole said. "Just like everybody else in town!"
"And some people from out of town too," Maggie added. "Look! Isn't that a Valley High T-shirt?"
She pointed to a teenage boy wearing a red-and-gold Valley High shirt. Valley High was the high school in a neighboring town.
Nathan pointed in a different direction. "That dark-haired girl Tina goes to Valley High too," he said. "She babysits my little sister sometimes."
"That's weird," Cole said. "Why would people from Valley High want to raise money for Belltown? They're our biggest rivals!"
"If you think that's weird, look at that guy." Maggie was staring at a man standing by himself.

Most of the riders were kids or teenagers. The adults were mostly teachers or coaches from Belltown High. But Henry didn't recognize this man. He was in his twenties, with very broad shoulders and dark sunglasses.
"Maybe he just likes bike riding," Henry said.
"He doesn't look very happy to be here," Cole said. "He's not smiling or talking to anyone."
Just then someone shouted for attention. It was Ms. Hernandez, the girls' soccer coach. "Is everyone ready to have some fun?" she called.
That made Henry forget about everything else. The ride was about to start!
"I'll be leading the ride," Ms. Hernandez said. "Remember, this isn't a race. Everyone who finishes gets a prize."
"Even if it takes me until tomorrow?" Cole called out.
Lots of people laughed, including Ms. Hernandez. "Even then," she said. "Let's get on the trail!"
"Go, Belltown!" a blond girl cried.
Henry recognized the girl. Her name was Melanie, and she was a cheerleader at Belltown High.
Today Melanie wasn't the only person cheering. Almost everyone let out a whoop as the bikers started down the trail.
Henry was trying to keep up with Cole and Maggie through some pine trees when a shiny mountain bike rushed in front of him.
"Whoa!" Henry cried. He braked just in time to keep from crashing into the other bike.
The rider was about his age. "Sorry," the boy muttered, glancing back at Henry. Then he rode ahead quickly.
Henry's friends had heard Henry cry out. They stopped and turned around to see if he was okay.
"Who was that kid?" Maggie asked.
A girl named Daisy overheard her. "Are you talking about that boy on the fancy mountain bike?" she asked.
"Yeah," Cole said. "We didn't recognize him."
"He just moved here," Daisy said. "His name is William. My mom told me his family bought a huge house right outside of town."
"How does she know?" asked Maggie.
"She sells houses for a living," Daisy explained.
A few more riders rode past, including Jill and Ashley. "Giving up already?" Jill called out to Henry and the others with a grin.
"No way!" Cole called back. "Come on, guys. Let's go!"

He raced off. Henry and Maggie chased after him, laughing. All three of them kept riding fast for a while. Then they slowed down to rest their legs. Lots of other people were riding slowly too, enjoying the pretty scenery.
"This is fun," Maggie said. "I'm glad we came."
"Even though it cost you ten dollars?" Cole teased.
"Maybe more than that," Maggie reminded him. "With all the lemonade business we lost today!"
Henry laughed, and then looked around.
"Where's Nathan? I haven't seen him since we started riding."
"I think he was behind us," Cole said. "Let's wait for him to catch up."
They stopped their bikes. Lots of other riders passed them. Most were smiling or chatting with their friends. Everyone seemed to be having fun.
Then William rode past again. He wasn't smiling or talking to anyone.
"He doesn't look like he's having a good time," Cole whispered.
Henry didn't answer. He'd just spotted Nathan coming. He wasn't smiling either. The teenage boy in the Valley High shirt was riding alongside him.
"What's the matter?" the older boy teased Nathan. "Can't you keep up? Is everyone at Belltown High School as slow and lazy as you?"
Henry could tell that Nathan was trying to ignore the bully. But just then Nathan bumped into a rock on the trail. His front tire wobbled, and he had to brake suddenly.
"Looks like you're quitting," the bully said with a smirk. "I guess that makes you a Belltown quitter!"
"Hey!" Cole said. "Leave him alone!"
Just then three other riders caught up to them. They all went to Belltown High School. One was Henry's neighbor, Tiny, the tallest kid in tenth grade. "What's going on?" Tiny asked.
"That Valley High kid is bothering Nathan," Maggie said.
The bully heard her and scowled. "I was just joking around," he muttered.
One of Tiny's friends laughed. "That makes sense, since Valley High's sports teams are all a big joke."
"They are not!" the bully retorted angrily. " Yours are!"
He sped away, still scowling. The others shrugged and continued the ride. The trail wound through the woods, up and down hills, and past wildflower meadows. Finally it widened into a big field.
Many people had already stopped their bikes there.
"This must be the first rest stop," Henry said. There were two stops planned during the ride. A local restaurant was providing drinks and snacks for all the riders at each stop.
Henry and the others left their bikes in the field and walked up a narrow hiking trail. It took about five minutes to reach a picnic area near the river.

For the next half hour, everyone rested and enjoyed the snacks and the view. Henry sat with Cole, Maggie, Nathan, and some other friends. He noticed William sitting by himself and wondered if he should invite William to sit with them.
Before Henry could decide, William got up and wandered away.
Finally Ms. Hernandez announced that it was time to continue the ride. But when they got back to the bikes, someone let out a cry of surprise.
"I can't believe this!" Daisy shouted. "Someone slashed our tires!"
"No way! Who would slash our bike tires?" Maggie cried, rushing over to her bicycle. "Wait," she added. "I think my tires are okay."
"Mine too," someone else called out.
Henry checked his bike. His tires were fine. "It looks like only some tires were slashed," he said.
"Yeah. Like mine!" Cole sounded upset as he looked at his tires. "Who would be mean enough to do this?"
"I don't know," Henry said. "But maybe The Lemonade Detectives can figure it out."

He looked around, trying to see how everyone was reacting. Most of the riders looked confused or upset. A bunch of kids were gathered around Ms. Hernandez, asking her questions about what had happened. Then Henry spotted the man in the dark glasses. He was standing by his bike with his arms folded, looking bored.
Maggie noticed him too. "Hey, maybe it was that guy!" she whispered. "I didn't see him while we were at the picnic spot. He could have been down here slashing tires the whole time!"
"Maybe," Henry said. "I didn't notice him while we were up there either."
"I bet it was those kids from Valley High School," said Cole. "They probably came on the ride to make trouble!"
Henry looked around for the Valley High teens. He couldn't see the girl in the crowd, but he spotted the boy right away. He was smirking as he watched everyone check their tires.
"His tires look okay," Cole said. "And we already know he doesn't like Belltown. Remember how he was teasing Nathan?"
"Yeah. He should be a suspect too," Henry said. "Did anyone see him at the picnic area?"
"I didn't," Maggie said. "So that proves it! He's guilty!"

As usual, Maggie was jumping to conclusions. "It doesn't prove anything," Henry reminded her. "There were lots of people I didn't notice while we were at the picnic area. We should start questioning everyone and see who left."
"I remember someone who left!" Maggie said. "That rich kid, William. I saw him get up and walk toward the path leading down here."
Henry remembered seeing William leave the picnic area too. "Okay," he said. "But that doesn't prove anything either. Lots of people left to walk down to the restrooms."
Just then Jill and Ashley rushed over. "This is terrible!" Ashley cried. "Someone's trying to ruin our fundraiser!"
"You have to help us," Jill added. "We want to hire The Lemonade Detectives to solve this horrible crime!"
Henry smiled. "I don't know if I'd call it a horrible crime," he said.
"But don't worry. We're already on the case. To start, we want to question you two."
"What?" Jill looked outraged. "You don't suspect us again , do you?"
"No!" Henry said quickly. "You're not suspects this time."

He knew why Jill was annoyed. Somehow she ended up being a suspect in a lot of The Lemonade Detectives' cases. Ashley had been a suspect once too. Henry was pretty sure that they were innocent again now. Why would they try to ruin a fundraiser for their own team?
"So what do you want to ask us?" Ashley asked.
"Do you know how many bikes got damaged?" Henry asked.
Ashley shrugged. "We're not sure exactly," she said. "We'll have to check with Ms. Hernandez. But at least six or seven bikes have slashed tires."
"We were just trying to figure out who left the picnic spot," Cole added. "Did you notice anyone slipping away?"
"Oh." Jill looked less upset now that she realized she wasn't a suspect. "I don't know. I wasn't paying much attention to that."
"Yeah," Ashley said. "I walked down to the restrooms with a couple of friends. The only person there when we left was your friend Nathan."
Henry nodded, remembering that Nathan had gone to the restroom alone. He was sure his friend hadn't slashed those tires. But maybe Nathan had seen something suspicious.
"Thanks," Henry said. "We'd better start investigating. What are you going to do about the ride?"
"Good question." Cole frowned as he looked at his bike again. "I can't ride with a slashed tire."
"I think Ms. Hernandez is calling Belltown Bikes." Ashley glanced over at the coach, who was talking on her cell phone. "She's going to ask them to bring new tires to replace the slashed ones."
"Good," Henry said. "That should give us some time to question people before the ride continues."
"Yeah." Jill didn't look happy. "But someone will have to pay for the new tires. So if you guys don't solve the mystery, we might not raise enough money to buy our uniforms!"

As Jill and Ashley hurried off, Henry looked at his friends. "We'll have to work fast if we want to solve this mystery," he said. "The ride will probably start up again after those new tires get here."
"Then let's not waste any time," Cole said. "Who should we question next?"
"How about William?" Maggie pointed to the new boy, who was kneeling by his front tire. "He's one of our suspects. And he's right over there."
The Lemonade Detectives walked over to William. "Hi," Henry greeted him. "Did your tire get slashed?"
"Yes!" William scowled. "And it was really expensive."

Just then Ms. Hernandez called for everyone’s attention. "I spoke to Belltown Bikes," she announced. "They'll be here in about 15 minutes with replacement tires. The ride will continue once everyone's bike is fixed, so please be patient."
"That doesn't give us much time," said Cole.
Henry nodded. He turned to ask William another question, but the boy had disappeared while Ms. Hernandez was talking.
"That's odd," Henry thought.
Maggie had noticed too. "Hey, where did William go?" she asked.
Cole shrugged. "Never mind. We can't waste time looking for him now."
"Right," Henry agreed. "Let's split up so we can interview more people. Try to find out who left the picnic area, how long they were gone, and who was with them. We'll meet back here in 15 minutes."
His friends nodded and hurried off, and Henry looked around. Who should he talk to first? He saw Tiny and his friends nearby.
"Hi, Henry," Tiny greeted him. "How are your tires?"
"They're fine," Henry said. "What about yours?"
Tiny sighed. "I got my front and back tires slashed," he said, pointing to his bike. "Hey, you're a detective, right? Maybe you can figure out who did this!"
"I'm trying," Henry said. "I want to figure out who left the picnic area while we were all there."
"Not us." Tiny glanced at his friends. "But some of the girls we were sitting with went to the restroom."
"Did they all walk there together?" Henry asked.
One of Tiny's friends laughed. "Of course! Girls always go to the bathroom together."
"Yeah," Tiny agreed with a grin. "That way they can talk about us boys!"
Henry smiled. "Did you notice anyone else disappearing for a long time?"
"No." Tiny shrugged.
"Wait, I did," the other friend said. "It was that weird guy with the dark glasses."
"You're right," said Tiny's friend with the blond hair. "He's hard to miss! I think that kid from Valley High left for a while too." He rolled his eyes. "I don't like him at all."
Just then Daisy walked over. "Hi, Henry," she said. "Are The Lemonade Detectives trying to solve the case of the slashed tires?"
"Yes," Henry said.
"I just thought of something. What if it wasn't someone from the ride at all?" Tiny said. "This is a public park. It could have been anyone."
Daisy shook her head. "Who would follow us all the way out here just to slash our tires? Besides I bet I know who did it."
"Who?" Henry asked.
"That guy with the sunglasses," Daisy said. "Nobody knows who he is. Plus, he was only at the picnic area for a few minutes."
Henry saw a flash of red and gold. When he looked over, he saw the boy from Valley High School hurrying toward the restrooms. The other student from Valley High School, Tina, was following him.
"What about Tina?" he asked. "Did anyone notice if she left the picnic area?"
Daisy nodded. "I think I saw her leave for a while. She’s really nice. Is she a suspect?"
"I'm not sure yet," Henry said. "I need to get all the facts first."
He spent the next few minutes questioning several other people. Then it was time to meet the other Lemonade Detectives.
"What did you find out?" Henry asked when the three of them were together again.
"Almost everyone saw that guy with the sunglasses leave the picnic area," Maggie said. "A few people noticed that William left too, but nobody saw him come back."
"Hmm . . . ," said Henry.
"I found out the same thing," said Cole. "I also found out that Joey and Tina, the two kids from Valley High, left for a while. What if they planned this prank to make Belltown look bad?"
"Maybe we should talk to them," Henry said.
He and his friends found Joey and Tina standing outside the restrooms. But they weren't laughing over the prank or plotting more trouble. Tina looked angry as she glared at Joey.
"I know you slashed those tires, and you'd better confess!" she yelled at him. "You're making our school look bad!"
"We knew it!" Maggie yelled at Joey. "You slashed those tires, didn't you?"
"It wasn't me!" Joey pointed at Tina. "She probably did it, and now she's trying to blame it on me!"
Tina gasped. "I did not do it!"
All the commotion was attracting attention.
"What's going on?" Ashley asked, hurrying over.
"This kid slashed the tires!" Maggie cried, pointing at Joey.
"I already told you dummies that I didn't do it!" Joey yelled.
Maggie glared at him. "Why should we believe you? We heard you teasing Nathan. So we already know you're a bully!"
More people had arrived by then. "Wait," the Belltown cheerleader named Melanie spoke up. "He's telling the truth. He didn't do it."
"How do you know?" Jill asked.
"Because I saw him hanging out right here by the restrooms," Melanie said. "I was down here for most of the break because I had a stomachache. He was here the whole time."
"Are you sure?" Ashley asked. "Maybe he sneaked away while you weren't looking."
Melanie laughed. "Are you kidding? Those Valley High colors are so bright you can't miss them. I would have noticed if he left even for a second."
"Oh." Ashley shrugged. "Okay, I guess he couldn't have slashed the tires after all."
Just then Ms. Hernandez arrived. "What's all the yelling over here?"
"Nothing," Jill said. "We were just talking."
Joey and Tina stomped off in opposite directions. Soon most of the other kids wandered away.
Henry led his friends to a private spot. "I guess Joey didn't do it," he said. "He has an alibi."
"What's an alibi?" Maggie asked.

"It's when someone can prove that he or she wasn’t at the scene of the crime," Henry said. "Joey's alibi is that Melanie saw him by the restrooms. That means he couldn't have been down at the bikes slashing tires."
"Okay," Maggie said. "I guess he's not the culprit. But what about Tina? Melanie didn't say anything about seeing her."
"Yeah. And a few people said she disappeared for a while," Cole added.

"She's still a suspect, I guess," Henry said. "But we shouldn't focus only on the Valley High kids. There are other suspects." Just then he spotted the stranger in the sunglasses walking along, muttering into a cell phone. "Like him, for instance," he whispered. "Did either of you question him earlier?"
"Nope," Maggie said while Cole shook his head.
"Let's talk to him now," Henry said.
They hurried after the man, who was heading toward the bike rack. On the way they passed Ms. Hernandez talking to William. He looked upset.
"Why can't I leave now?" he whined. "My bike is ruined, and I want to go home."
Ms. Hernandez sighed. "Please be patient. The new tires will be here soon."
"They probably won't even fit my bike," William argued. "Anyway this ride is no fun."
"Why does he want to quit the bike ride?" Maggie whispered. "Maybe he feels guilty because he committed the crime."
"But his tire got slashed too," Cole whispered. "Why would he ruin his own tire?"
"Maybe he did it so nobody would suspect him," Henry said. "We can question him after we talk to the mystery man."
They kept going. The man in the sunglasses stopped near his own bike and finished up his call.
"Hi," Henry said, walking up to the man. "It looks like your tires didn't get slashed, huh? That's lucky."
The man shrugged. "I suppose so. But only nine tires were damaged."
Henry traded a look with his friends. How did this man know exactly how many tires had been slashed? It seemed suspicious.
"How did you hear about this bike ride?" Cole asked. "Most of the riders are from the Belltown schools. I didn't know other people even knew about it."
The man looked away. "News gets around, I guess," he muttered.

Henry could tell he didn't want to answer their questions. That seemed suspicious too. Luckily Henry's father worked as a reporter at the local newspaper. He'd taught Henry a few interviewer's tricks. One trick was rewording the same question in a different way.
"Did you see a flyer hanging up around town?" he asked. "I bet that's how you heard about the ride. Or maybe you have a relative that goes to Belltown High."
"Not exactly." The man looked annoyed. "Actually I'm a news reporter. I'm here to cover the story for the local paper."
"What?" Maggie exclaimed. "But . . ."
Henry elbowed her in the ribs before she could say anything more. A second later the stranger hurried off.
Cole looked confused. "What was that all about? Does that man work with your dad, Henry?"
"No," Henry said. "I know all the reporters at the paper, and that guy isn't one of them. He's lying!"
"Now what do we do?" Cole asked, staring after the mystery man. "Do you think he's the culprit?"
Maggie frowned. "I don't get it. Nobody here knows him. Why would some stranger slash our tires?"
"People get robbed by strangers all the time," Cole pointed out.
"That's different," Henry said. "Robbers have a motive. They want the money or other stuff that they steal. What's that guy's motive for slashing our tires?"
"I don't know," Cole said. "But I think the new tires are here."
A van was pulling into the field. It had the Belltown Bikes logo painted on the side. Several of the bike shop's employees jumped out and started helping people replace their tires.
Before long all the bikes were fixed. Ms. Hernandez made the riders line up so she could make sure everyone was there. Then she got on her bike. "Time to get back on the trail!" she called out.
"Hip, hip, hooray!" Melanie cheered, jumping up and down. "Go, Belltown!"
Soon Henry was back on the trail. But he wasn't paying attention to the scenery. He was still thinking about the mystery.
"We need to keep working on this case," he told Maggie and Cole.
"Why?" Maggie asked. "That mystery man probably did it. Why else would he lie to us about being a newspaper reporter?"
"I don't know," Henry said. "He might have other reasons."
Cole nodded. "Yeah. Maybe he's a spy!"

Henry doubted that. But he had a feeling The Lemonade Detectives were missing an important clue. "Let's split up and talk to people again," he said. "If we can prove everybody else didn't do it, we can investigate that mystery man."

They spent the next few minutes talking to people as they rode along. Henry questioned different riders about what they'd seen during the break. The more he learned, the more he realized that most riders had alibis. Either they hadn't left the picnic area, or they'd been with other people when they had.
Then he caught up to William. "I guess Ms. Hernandez talked him out of quitting," he thought.
"Hi, William," Henry called. "Are you having fun?"
William looked over at him. "Sure, I guess so."
"Good," Henry said. "Because I heard you talking to Ms. Hernandez earlier. Why did you want to quit partway through the ride?"

William looked surprised and then annoyed. "None of your business," he muttered. Then he sped up and rode off. His fancy mountain bike could go really fast. Henry was wondering whether he should try to catch up when he heard Maggie.
"Henry! Wait up!"
A second later she and Cole both caught up to him. The three of them discussed what they'd found out.
"It seems like there are only five people who don't have alibis for the time of the crime," Henry said. "Nathan, Ms. Hernandez, Tina, William, and the mystery man."
"We know Nathan would never slash people's tires," Cole said.
Henry nodded. "I think we can cross Ms. Hernandez off the list too. That leaves three suspects: Tina, William, and the mystery man."
"I still think Tina did it," Cole said. "Why would she come on the ride to raise money for Belltown High unless she wanted to cause trouble?"
"I don't know," Henry said. "But we can't assume it was her. We thought it was Joey, and he had an alibi, remember?"
He rode around a curve in the trail. He was thinking so hard, it took him a second to spot the rider stopped by the side of the trail. It was Nathan. He was standing beside his bike, looking worried.
The Lemonade Detectives stopped beside him. "What's wrong?" Maggie asked.
"It's my bike." Nathan pointed toward the gears. "The chain fell off! And I don't know how to fix it. Can you guys help?"
Henry shook his head. "I don't know how to fix it either." He looked at Maggie and Cole. "What about you two?"
They shook their heads too. "Maybe you can leave your bike here and ride double with one of us," Maggie suggested.

Just then Joey rode toward them. He smirked when he saw them. "Having bike trouble, Belltown losers?" he yelled. "Good, you deserve it!" He sped around the next curve, making dirt fly at them as he passed.
"Go back to Valley High, you bully!" Maggie yelled.
"Forget about him." Nathan sighed. "What am I going to do about my bike?"
A few more riders rounded the curve. Some of them looked over at Nathan's broken bike. But nobody stopped.
Then Tina rode into view. As soon as she saw Nathan's bike, she steered toward him. "Your chain fell off, huh?" she said with a friendly smile. "Don't worry. I can help you fix it."
"Can you really fix my bike?" Nathan asked Tina. "Thanks!"
"You're welcome. This will only take a second."
Tina bent over the bike and expertly put the chain back in place. Then she turned the pedals to test it.
"Good as new," she said. "It should be fine now."
"Thank you so much!" Nathan exclaimed. "I really appreciate it."
"No problem. Enjoy the rest of the ride!" With a friendly wave to all of them, Tina pedaled off.
"Wow," Maggie said. "That was really nice of her."
Cole nodded. "Yeah, and she's one of our suspects," he said. "Would someone who just slashed a bunch of tires do something nice like that?"
"I'm glad you guys are trying to figure out who slashed those tires," Nathan said. "That means it won't be long until the mystery is solved. The Lemonade Detectives solve all their cases!"
He rode off, humming happily. Henry frowned, realizing that Nathan was right.
"It's true," he said. "We've solved every case so far. But this one might be our toughest yet."
Maggie looked worried. "You're right. What if we can't solve it before the ride is over? The Lemonade Detectives' reputation will be ruined!"
"And so will the soccer team's fundraiser," Cole said. "But don't worry. We already have it narrowed down to three suspects, remember?"
"Or maybe two," Henry said. "It's hard to believe Tina is the culprit. She seems too nice. And she seemed pretty mad when she accused Joey of slashing the tires earlier."
"But why would she help raise money for Belltown?" Maggie said. "That doesn't make sense."
"I don't know," Henry said. "But I know someone who might be able to tell us. I just remembered I saw Tina sitting with Daisy for a while during the break."
"Oh yeah, I noticed that too," Cole said. "I was surprised that Tina wasn't sitting with that Joey guy since they're both from Valley High. Do you think Tina and Daisy are friends?"
"There's only one way to find out," Henry replied. "Let's go ask Daisy."
They rode ahead until they caught up with Daisy. Maggie jumped right into questioning her. "We saw you sitting with that girl from Valley High earlier," she said to Daisy. "Do you know her?"
"You mean Tina?" Daisy nodded. "We went to the same summer camp last year. She's cool."
"Is that why she came on this ride?" Cole asked. "Because you two are friends?"

Daisy shrugged. "I'm the one who told her about the fundraiser. But she probably would have heard about it anyway. She's a really serious rider. She trains all the time, and she enters every local ride and race she can find."
"Oh, that explains why she's here!" Henry said. "It also explains how she knew how to fix Nathan's bike."
"Wait a minute," Daisy said. "You don't suspect Tina of slashing those tires, do you? Because she'd never do something like that. She loves bikes, plus she's really nice."
"Yeah. We just figured that out." Henry smiled. "Don't worry. She's off our list of suspects."
He, Maggie, and Cole rode off by themselves. "So now we only have two suspects," Cole said. "William and the mystery man."
"Both of them have been acting suspicious all day," Maggie said.
"But neither has a good motive," Henry pointed out. "At least not one we know about."
"William isn't having much fun on this ride," Maggie said. "He acts like he doesn't even want to be here."

"And he tried to convince Ms. Hernandez to let him quit at the first rest break," Cole said. "Maybe he slashed the tires because he thought the rest of the ride would be canceled. Then when it wasn't, he had to figure out another way to quit early."
"Why would he come on the ride at all if he didn't want to be here?" Maggie wondered. "Do you think his parents made him come?"
"I don't know," Henry said. "But I can't stop thinking about how that guy lied to us about being a reporter. Why would he do that?"
"Good question," Maggie said. "I just don't know how we're going to figure it out. He won't tell us anything. And nobody else here knows anything about him."

Soon they reached the next rest area. Henry coasted to a stop behind the other bikes. This picnic area was right beside a parking lot. That was good since it meant that nobody could touch the bikes without being seen.
"We'd better figure out how to solve this case," Henry said. "We're almost out of time."
Henry, Maggie, and Cole walked over to the picnic tables. People from a local restaurant were passing out snacks and drinks.

Henry took a bottle of water, but he felt too worried to eat a snack. What if The Lemonade Detectives couldn't solve this case before the end of the ride? So far they'd done everything detectives were supposed to do. They'd figured out suspects, motives, and alibis. But they still hadn't solved the case.
"Let's split up and question our last two suspects," Henry told his friends.
"Okay," Cole agreed. "I'll try to talk to the mystery man if you want."
"Fine. Maggie and I will find William."
They split up and started searching. The picnic area was crowded. At first Henry didn't see either of their suspects.
Then Maggie grabbed his arm. "There's William."
Henry looked toward where she was pointing. William was sitting by himself, staring out at the woods and eating an apple.
"Let's decide what we're going to say before we go over," Henry said.
"We don't have time," Maggie said impatiently. "Let's just go tell him we know he did it. If he's guilty, he might confess."

"I'm not sure that will work." Henry glanced at William. The new boy looked bored and lonely. Even though William was a suspect, Henry felt a little sorry for him. It couldn't be easy being the new kid in town.
"Look, his bag is on the table behind him," Maggie said. "Come on, I have a plan!"

"A plan? What is it?" Henry felt worried. Maggie wasn't usually the type of person who came up with logical, well-thought-out plans. She was the type of person who acted first and thought about it later.
"There's no time to explain," Maggie said. "Just talk to him to distract him, and I'll take care of the rest."
"Maggie, wait!" Henry said.
It was too late. Maggie was already rushing toward the picnic table where William was sitting. Henry followed, hoping that her plan would work, whatever it was.
William looked up when he saw them coming. He didn't look particularly happy to see them.
"Hi," Henry said, trying to sound friendly. "That apple looks good. Where did you get it?"
"Over there," William said, pointing to a basket that the restaurant people had set out.
"Oh . . . great . . ." Henry was running out of things to say. He shot a desperate look at Maggie. She flopped down on the bench across from William.
"Whew!" she exclaimed dramatically. "I'm so tired!"
She flung her arms out. One knocked into William's unzipped bag and sent it flying. The contents scattered everywhere.
"Hey!" William exclaimed. "You spilled all my stuff!"
"Sorry," Maggie said, leaping down and grabbing the bag. She shook it upside down. "Oops, you're right. Everything fell out! But don't worry, I'll clean it up."
Henry and William watched as she picked up all the spilled items. There was a cell phone, a house key, and a few other things.
"There." Maggie zipped the bag shut. "All fixed."
"Thanks," William muttered. "Um, did you guys want to sit here, or what?"
"Maybe later," Maggie said. "Come on, Henry. Let's go find Cole."
The two of them made their escape. "What was that all about?" Henry asked as soon as they were out of William's earshot.

Maggie smiled. "Don't you get it? There was nothing in that bag that William could have used to slash the tires. And his bike shorts don't have pockets, so he couldn't be carrying a penknife or anything that way."
"I suppose you're right," Henry agreed. "But how do you know he didn't drop the crime weapon in the woods after he used it?"
Maggie's face fell. "I didn't think of that." She frowned. "Why do you always have to be so logical?"
"Never mind. It was still a pretty good plan," Henry said. "If there had been a penknife in there, it would've worked."
"That's true." Maggie looked a little happier. "So should we go back and try to talk to William some more?"
Before Henry could answer, he saw Cole rushing toward them, looking excited. "Big news!" he cried when he reached them.
"Did you talk to the mystery man?" Henry asked.
Cole shook his head. "I never found him," he said breathlessly. "But I did find out more about him. And about William too."
"Really?" Maggie said. "Like what?"
"Like William's family isn't just rich," Cole said. "His dad works for the government. He's a senator in the United States Senate!"
"Really?" Henry said. "Wow. That's cool."
Cole nodded. "But that's not all," he said. "Everyone has noticed that the mystery man follows William everywhere. What if he's planning to kidnap William and hold him for ransom?"
"You think that mystery man wants to kidnap William?" Henry wasn't so sure about Cole's idea. "That kind of thing doesn't happen in Belltown."
"Daisy said William's family is rich," Cole said. "Or maybe the mystery man is mad about something William's dad did as a senator. And that's why he wants to kidnap William!"
Maggie looked excited. "This could be our biggest case yet!"
"But what does kidnapping have to do with slashing tires?" Henry asked.
"Maybe the mystery man was trying to distract everyone so he'd have a chance to nab William," said Cole.

"Maybe." Henry thought for a second. Then he shook his head. "I'm still not sure I believe any of this. But Maggie is right about one thing. This case is much more serious than our usual cases. We should warn William right away. Then we need to tell Ms. Hernandez."
Cole nodded. "Let's go find William."
The Lemonade Detectives wandered through the crowd, but William was nowhere to be seen.
Finally Maggie spotted him. He'd wandered off by himself into the woods.
They jogged toward him.
William saw them coming. "Oh, it's you," he said uneasily. "Did you come to knock over my bag again?"
"No, we came to warn you that someone might be trying to kidnap you," Cole said. "Have you noticed that stranger with the dark glasses?"
"He's been following you!" Maggie added. "We're afraid he wants to kidnap you for ransom."
For a second William just stared at them. Then he started laughing.
Henry was confused. That definitely wasn't the reaction he was expecting!
"What's so funny?" he asked.
William kept laughing. Then he turned and walked away.
"Hold on a minute!" Maggie stomped after him. "We're trying to help you! The least you can do is tell us what's so funny!"
"Okay." William finally stopped laughing. "You don't have to worry. That guy isn't trying to kidnap me."
"How do you know?" Henry asked.
For a second he thought William was going to walk away again.
Then Maggie poked William in the shoulder. "Tell us!" she ordered.
"While you're at it, tell us why you're here," Cole added. "We know you didn't want to come on this ride."
William frowned. "I did want to come," he said. "Well, I wanted to come at first. I thought it would be a good way to meet people since I'm new around here."
Henry nodded. "That makes sense. But you don't look like you're having much fun."
"That's because of Chuck," William said.
"Who's Chuck?" Maggie asked.
"The guy with the dark glasses." William hesitated. "He's my . . ."
"Your what?" Maggie prompted him.
William sighed. "My bodyguard."
"What?" Cole exclaimed.

"My parents made him come with me," William said. "We're new here so they weren't sure if the trail ride was safe for me. I didn't want everyone to think I was some weird rich kid with a bodyguard. So I decided not to come at all. But then my parents wouldn't let me back out." He shrugged. "Chuck promised he'd try to blend in with the other riders. But it didn't really work."
Maggie giggled. "Yeah. He sort of stands out in the crowd."
That made the others laugh too. Even William smiled.
Now Henry understood why Chuck had lied to them about being a reporter. He'd been trying to protect William.
William suddenly looked nervous. "Are you guys going to tell everyone?"
"No way," Cole said. "Your secret's safe with us."
Maggie nodded. "You can trust us. We're professionals."
"Professional what?" William asked.
"Detectives," Henry said. "Which reminds me—we have to hurry if we want to solve this case!"
"What case? We have no suspects!" Maggie reminded him.
"Maybe we can interview everyone again," Cole said. "Someone must have seen something suspicious!"
"What about those two kids who keep sneaking into the woods together?" William asked. "That seems kind of suspicious."
"What two kids?" Henry asked.
William shrugged. "I don't know who they are. Some teenage guy and girl wearing school T-shirts."
"Hi, guys," Nathan said, walking over. "What's going on?"
"We were just talking to William," Henry said. "William, this is Nathan."
"Hi." Nathan was friendly to everyone. "Are you new in Belltown?"
Henry left the two of them chatting and dragged his friends aside. "Who do you think William saw sneaking around?" he said. "Did we miss some suspects?"
"Maybe." Maggie shrugged. "But it was probably just high school kids sneaking away to kiss."
Just then Henry heard the sound of rustling leaves deeper in the woods.
Cole heard it too. "What's that? A deer or something?"
Henry saw a flash of bright red and gold through the trees. "No, it's a Valley High person—or people. Come on. This could be our last chance!"
"Wait a minute!" Maggie said. "I thought the Valley High kids were innocent!"
"Joey has an alibi since Melanie saw him at the restrooms," Henry replied. "And Tina seems too nice to be guilty. But William said the kids he saw sneaking around were wearing school T-shirts!"
"Lots of people are wearing Belltown High shirts," Cole pointed out. "How do you know William meant Valley High ones?"

"I don't," Henry said. "But we're out of other suspects. Maybe Tina and Joey are plotting against Belltown after all. She could have slashed those tires. And Joey could have hung around the restrooms to make sure nobody went down the trail and caught her."
"Ooh! That's sneaky!" Maggie exclaimed.
"Come on!" Henry cried. "Before we lose them!"

The Lemonade Detectives took off, following the sounds of running feet and crunching leaves. Every once in a while they spotted a new flash of red and gold. But Henry still couldn't see who they were chasing.
Finally they burst into a clearing. Two people were running across it, but only one of them was wearing a Valley High T-shirt. To Henry's surprise they were holding hands.
"Stop!" Henry yelled. "We see you!"
The two people dropped hands and spun around. "Leave us alone!" the boy yelled.
"It's Joey!" Maggie exclaimed.
Cole gasped. "And Melanie !"
Henry was surprised too. What was the Belltown cheerleader doing with the Valley High bully?
"Are you two boyfriend and girlfriend?" Maggie blurted out.
"Please don't tell anyone!" Melanie begged. "My parents think I'm too young to have a boyfriend. Plus everyone at Belltown High will be mad if they know I'm dating someone from Valley High."
Aha! Now Henry got it.
"It was you, wasn't it?" he asked Joey. "You slashed those tires. Then you asked your secret girlfriend to provide your alibi!"
Melanie gasped. "How did you know?" she cried.
"I didn't until right now," Henry admitted.
Maggie frowned. "Why did you slash everyone's tires?"
"Those dumb kids from Belltown made me mad," Joey said with a scowl. "They said Valley High's sports teams were a joke!"

Henry remembered hearing Tiny and his friends kidding around about that earlier in the day. "That's because you were picking on Nathan," he told Joey. "Anyway you still shouldn't have slashed anyone's tires."
"It's all her fault," Joey muttered, pointing at Melanie. "She talked me into coming on this stupid bike ride."
"What?" Melanie exclaimed. "How can you say that? I just wanted to spend time together!"

Now Henry understood everything. Melanie's parents wouldn't let her go out with Joey. So she'd talked Joey into coming to the bike ride so they could be together in secret. That's why William had seen them sneaking away a few times during the ride. But then Joey had ruined everything by losing his temper and slashing the tires.
"Whatever," Joey muttered. "You guys better not tell anyone, or else!"
"Or else what?" a deep voice asked.
It was Chuck the bodyguard! He'd just stepped into the clearing.
Joey looked surprised. "Who are you?"
"I'm the person who's going to make sure that you pay for those slashed tires." Chuck grabbed Joey by the arm. "Come on, kid. You too, blondie," he added, glancing at Melanie.
"Yes, sir," she said meekly, scurrying along as Chuck dragged Joey away.
Watching the scene, Maggie grinned. "I guess that's another case closed," she said. "The Lemonade Detectives keep their perfect record!"
The next day at the lemonade stand, Henry and his friends were still talking about the case. "I heard Melanie broke up with Joey," Cole said.
"Good," Maggie said. "He's not very nice."
"I'm glad he'll have to pay for those tires," Henry said. "That means the soccer team gets to keep all the money they raised."
Henry noticed William hurrying toward them. "Hi," William said. "I heard I'd find you guys here."
"Want some lemonade?" Maggie poured some into a cup. "For you, it's on the house."
"Thanks." William took a sip. "I'm on my way to Nathan's house to hang out. But I wanted to stop and thank you again for being so friendly to me."
"You're welcome," Henry said. "Tell Chuck thanks again for his help. If he hadn't come along when he did, Joey might have decided to beat us up to keep us quiet."
"He’s just glad you kept our secret," William said. "And guess what? He helped me convince my parents that I don't need a bodyguard for most of the stuff I do around town!"
"That's great." Henry smiled, glad that William seemed happier. "Don't worry, you can tell them that Belltown is a pretty safe place."
"Yeah." Cole grinned. "Especially with The Lemonade Detectives always on the job!"
"Look!" Maggie cried. "Do you think that's the van?"
Henry looked up from tying his shoelace. His cousin, Maggie, was jumping up and down and pointing down the street.
"William said that his parents were sending a blue van to pick us up," Henry said. "That must be the one."
Cole grabbed his backpack off the sidewalk. "I can't wait to get to the beach!" he exclaimed.

"Me neither," Henry agreed. Their new friend, William, had invited the three of them to spend the weekend at his family's beach house. It was on an island located about an hour's drive from Belltown, where they all lived.
The van stopped at the curb. A young woman was driving.
"Are you Henry, Maggie, and Cole?" she asked in a friendly voice.
"That's them!" someone called out from the back of the van. "Get in here, you guys!"
A second later the side door slid open. "Hi, Nathan," Henry said to the kid inside.
Nathan lived nearby and was one of the friendliest and happiest kids Henry knew. He was going to William's vacation house too.
"This is going to be great!" Cole said as he climbed into the van.
Maggie climbed in after him. "Yeah," she agreed. "But I wish I didn't have to close the lemonade stand for the whole weekend."
Cole made a face. "Are you kidding?" he said. "I'd much rather spend the weekend at the beach than pouring lemonade."

"Me too," Maggie said. "But I could make a lot of money selling lemonade this weekend. And I'm saving up right now. My barn is having a horse show at the end of the summer, and it costs a lot to compete in the show."
"You should have plenty of money for that," Cole said. "Our detective business has been booming lately. We solved the mystery of the missing baseball glove for Tiny last week."
Henry nodded. "And we helped Mr. Metz find his relatives' addresses so he could plan a family reunion. He paid us double our usual fee for that, remember?"

"I guess you're right." Maggie stared out the window, still thinking about the lemonade stand as the van pulled away. "Anyway, we'll be back on Monday. I hope everybody in Belltown is still thirsty when we get back."
Cole shrugged and then turned to Nathan and Henry. "Do you think we'll get to go surfing at William's beach house?" he wondered.
"I don't know," Nathan said. "I talked to William on the phone yesterday. But I didn't get to ask him many questions about this weekend. He sounded kind of weird."
"He sounded weird?" Henry said. "What do you mean?"
"He was quieter than usual." Nathan looked worried. "I hope he's not getting sick."
"Was he coughing and sneezing on the phone?" asked Cole.
"No. But my sister Nora has a really bad cold right now," Nathan said. "I guess that's what made me think of it."
"Let's talk about all the fun stuff we're going to do at the beach!" Maggie said, changing the subject.
"Yeah," Cole agreed. "Like swimming and bodysurfing . . ."
"Maybe we can do pirate things," Nathan suggested. "Pirates are cool!"
"I want to build a sand castle," Maggie said. "And look for seashells."
Henry grinned. "I can't wait to do all that stuff!"
"Here we are," the van driver said an hour later.

Henry looked out the window. They were approaching a large, fancy house. It sat near a sandy beach and was bigger than Henry's house and Maggie's house put together. In the distance Henry could see a long row of tall, rocky cliffs.
"Wow, this place is great!" Maggie exclaimed. "We're going to have so much fun."
"Look, there's William." Nathan pointed. A kid was standing in front of the house. A girl around his age was beside him.
As soon as the driver stopped the van, Henry and the others jumped out. "Hi, William," Henry said. "Thanks for inviting us!"
"You're welcome," William said. He pointed to the girl. "This is Anna. She lives here in Sea Cove."
"You live at the beach all year long? Cool!" said Cole. "I'm Cole."
"And I'm Henry," Henry said. "That's my cousin, Maggie, and that's Nathan."
"Nice to meet you," Anna said. "Is this your first time coming to—"
Suddenly a figure, waving a long, gleaming sword, leaped from behind a shrub. "Aargh!" he growled.
"Ahh!" Nathan yelled when the masked figure jumped in front of them.
Henry gasped. Maggie and Cole jumped back. But they were startled for only a second. The figure was just a kid in a pirate mask.
"Sorry I scared you," the kid said, pulling off his mask.
William grinned. "This is Luke," he told Henry and the others. "He's a friend from my old school."
"You must like pirates as much as Nathan does," Henry said.
Luke nodded eagerly. "That's one reason I like coming here. I love exploring Pirate Beach!"
"Pirate Beach?" Nathan echoed. "That's what this place is called?"
Anna rolled her eyes. "It's named after some stupid legend."
"The legend isn't stupid," Luke said. "Pirates used to land their ships here all the time. Some people think they hid their treasure on this beach."

"Wow!" Nathan looked impressed. "That sounds like something from a pirate movie. In fact, I just heard about a new movie coming out soon. It's called Revenge of the Pirate's Ghost, " he added. "I'm dying to see it!"
"Me too," Luke said.
Just then William's parents hurried out of the house. "Welcome!" William's mother said.
"We have an exciting weekend planned for you," added William's father. "How would you like to search for pirate booty?"
"Booty?" Maggie said. "What's that?"
"Booty is what pirates call treasure," Luke explained. He turned to William's parents. "Is it real pirates' booty?"
William's mother smiled. "Not exactly. We've created a treasure hunt for you."
"What?" William blurted out.
"Cool!" Nathan and Luke said at the same time.
"That sounds perfect for Nathan and Luke," said Cole. "They're both obsessed with pirates!"
"What's the treasure?" Maggie blurted out. "Is it gold?"

William's mother smiled. "You'll have to wait to see what the treasure is," she said. "But here's how the hunt will work: we'll give you a clue. You'll follow it to find a hidden treasure chest. Some booty will be hidden inside, along with your next clue."
"At the end of the treasure hunt, you'll find a big surprise!" her husband finished.
"Awesome!" Luke pumped his fist. "Let's get started!"
Everyone else looked excited too. Well, not everyone. Henry noticed that William didn't even seem to be paying attention. He was staring out at the ocean.
"Come on, Henry." Cole poked him in the arm. "It's time to find some pirate booty!"
After Henry and his friends dropped their luggage inside the house, William's father handed the clue to Anna. "Have fun, kids. We'll see you at lunchtime."
Outside, Nathan took the clue from Anna. "Let me see that," he said. "Luke and I are the pirate experts around here. I bet we can figure out where the first treasure is!"
"Right," Luke agreed. "I think we should—"
"Don't hog the map," Maggie said, snatching the paper away from Nathan. "Besides, we don't need pirate experts to find treasure. We need The Lemonade Detectives!"
"The what?" Anna sounded curious.
Cole started to tell her and Luke about the detective agency. But Henry was watching Nathan, who was scowling at Maggie.
"You're not the only ones who can figure out clues," Nathan complained. "And you shouldn't grab stuff out of other people's hands."
"Sorry," Maggie mumbled. She continued studying the map. "Doesn't it look like the first chest is hidden near those big pointy rocks?"
Henry looked at the map and then down at the beach where Maggie was pointing. "I think you're right! Let's go look."
They all ran down the beach toward the pointy rock formation. When they got closer, they spotted a man wandering along in the surf.
"Who's that?" Cole asked. As the man approached, they could see he had a bristly, reddish-brown beard and twinkling blue eyes.
"I don't know," William said. "But he shouldn't be here—this is private property."
The stranger had overheard William. "Private property, hmm?" he said with a chuckle. "It's a good thing my ancestor, Captain Roger Redbeard, isn't alive to hear you say that."
"Captain Roger Redbeard?" Nathan echoed. "That sounds like a pirate's name."
The man chuckled again. "That's because he was a pirate. He's the one Pirate Beach is named after."
"Cool!" Luke exclaimed. "Does that mean you're the relative of a real pirate?"
"That's right." The man nodded. "I'm even named after him. You can call me Roger."
Henry noticed that Maggie wasn't paying attention to Roger. She'd hurried ahead of everyone. She looked at the map again and then back down at the sand.
Then she dropped to her knees and started to dig with her hands. "I bet the treasure is right around here!"
"You found the spot where the treasure is buried?" Cole ran toward Maggie.
Henry and the others rushed after him. Even Roger wandered over, looking curious.
Maggie was still digging in the sand. Cole, Henry, Nathan, and Luke joined in. Soon they uncovered a large wooden trunk.
"It looks like a real pirate chest!" Nathan said. He looked at Roger. "Doesn't it?"
"Sure does." Roger winked. "Have fun with your treasure, kids. But watch out for Roger Redbeard!" He wandered off, whistling.
"What are we waiting for, you guys?" Cole said eagerly. "Let's find out what our booty is!"
Maggie opened the trunk. "Pirate hats!" she said.
Luke grabbed one and then handed another one to Henry. "This one has your name on it, Henry."
Cole pulled out more hats. "We each have one."
Nathan grinned and put on his hat. "Do I look like a pirate?"
Anna snorted. "You look like a kid with a dumb hat on to me," she said. Laughing, she tried her hat on too.
Henry put on his hat and glanced at William. William hadn't touched his hat. And instead of laughing at how silly everyone looked, William had an angry scowl on his face.
Henry moved closer to Cole. "Did you notice how strange William is acting today?" he whispered.
"No." Cole glanced toward William. "What do you mean?"
"He doesn't seem very excited about this treasure hunt," Henry whispered. "Do you think it's because he helped his parents hide the booty? Maybe he's trying not to give us any hints."

"Maybe." Cole shrugged. "Or maybe he's bored because he does cool stuff like this all the time. His family is really rich, remember?" Cole went on. "They might have fancy treasure hunts every weekend."
Meanwhile Luke had spotted a folded-up piece of paper inside the treasure chest. "I think this is our next clue," he said.
Maggie unfolded the piece of paper. It was a drawing of a blue object along the beach. "What do you think this is supposed to be?" she murmured.
"A swimming pool?" said Cole.
"It looks like a little pond," said Henry.
"Or a tide pool!" said Anna. "I bet that's what it is."
Luke glanced around the beach. "Where's the closest one?" he asked.
"Hmm . . . ," Anna said, thinking. "There are at least four tide pools near here. We should split up and check all of them."
"Nathan and I will search together," Luke said.
"I'll go with Henry," Maggie said.
"Okay," Anna said. "I can search alone, since I know this beach better than anyone else."
"I guess that leaves you and me," Cole told William with a grin.
Anna told each pair where to go. Then the kids set out in different directions.
It took Henry and Maggie about half an hour to find their tide pool and look for the treasure. But they didn't find anything.
"Let's go see if the others found the treasure," Maggie said.
They returned to the beach in front of the house. Cole was already there.
"Did you find the booty?" Maggie asked him.
"Nope," Cole said. "Did you?"
Henry shook his head. "Where's William?" he asked.
"William left right after we all split up," Cole replied. "He said he had to use the bathroom. But he never came back." Cole frowned, looking annoyed. "I had to find our tide pool all by myself."
Before Henry could respond, he saw Anna walking toward them. "No luck, huh?" she asked. "Me neither."
Just then they all heard a shout. It was Nathan. He was racing down the beach toward them, waving his arms.
"We found it!" he cried. He skidded to a stop and then bent over to catch his breath. He started coughing.
"Take it easy," Cole said. "Did you say you found the booty?"

Nathan nodded. When he finally stopped coughing, he said, "Luke and I had some trouble finding our tide pool. But when we got there, we spotted something in the water right away. Come on, I'll show you."
Henry, Maggie, Anna, and Cole followed him down the beach. When they reached Nathan's tide pool, Maggie gasped. "It's tear-shaped—like the picture on the map!"
Luke was fishing a plastic container out of the water. William was there, watching him.
"Is that the treasure?" Maggie wondered, eying the box. "It's pretty small."
"Open it," Nathan urged.
Luke opened the container. Then he frowned. "This can't be the treasure."
"Why not?" Henry asked. "What's wrong?"
Luke held the container out so they could all see inside. "There's nothing in here except a few soggy sticks of gum!"
"Gum?" Cole said in surprise. "Are you sure that's all that's in there?"
"Yeah," said Maggie. "Is our next clue in there?"
"Um . . . let's see." Luke turned the container upside down and shook it. Some tissue paper fluttered out. Then a folded piece of paper fell out.

Maggie picked up the folded paper. "It's another clue. So this is definitely the right box," she said. "Hey, William, why would your parents give us a few lousy sticks of gum? That's not much of a treasure."
"Shh," Henry shushed her. Maggie was being rude.
"It is kind of weird," Cole said. "Do pirates even chew gum?"
Nathan shrugged. "I don't think so," he said. "I doubt they can get it on the high seas."
Luke laughed. "Maybe they steal it from the ships they raid." He tilted his pirate hat and then pretended to swing his sword. "Ahoy, mateys! Give me your gum, or I'll make you walk the plank!"
Nathan pretended to fight back with an invisible sword. "No way!" he cried. "I'll die before I hand over my gum!"
"Stop messing around, you guys," Maggie said. "Seriously, why would William's parents give us gum? It doesn't fit in with the pirate theme at all."
Henry didn't say anything, but he had to agree.

"Oh well." Cole grabbed one of the sticks of gum. "At least we can chew gum while we follow the next clue." Then he looked at the gum and wrinkled his nose. "Yuck," he added. "Never mind. It's watermelon. I hate that flavor."
"Watermelon? Cool!" Luke grabbed another stick of gum. "That's my favorite. I buy this gum at the general store every time I come here. Anna's store is the only place I know that sells this brand."
"Your family owns a general store?" Maggie asked Anna.
"Great deduction, detective Maggie," Nathan said sarcastically.

Henry was surprised by Nathan's remark. "Is Nathan still mad at Maggie for grabbing the map away from him earlier?" Henry thought. That wasn't like Nathan at all. He almost never got mad. And even if he did, he didn't stay mad for long.
"My family's store is one of the oldest businesses in Sea Cove," Anna told Maggie. "My great-grandfather started the store a long time ago. Everyone in town shops there."
Luke grinned and blew a bubble. "Yeah. They have the best gum in town!"
Cole tossed his gum back into the container. "I still think a few sticks of gum is a weird prize," he said. "Especially for a pirate treasure hunt. Are you sure we found the right box, William?"
"How should I know?" William snapped with a frown. "I didn't have anything to do with this stupid scavenger hunt."
Cole looked surprised. "Okay," he said.
Henry bit his lip. Everyone seemed a little grouchy right now.
"Why don't we go see if lunch is ready?" he suggested. "Maybe we can ask William's parents about the gum."
"Good idea," Cole agreed. "All this treasure hunting has made me hungry."

They headed back to the house. A lunch of sandwiches and juice was set out on the deck. William's parents were there too, sipping tall glasses of iced tea. As the kids sat down to eat, they told William's parents about how the treasure hunt was going so far. When they got to the part about the gum, William's mother looked surprised.
"Gum?" she said. "I didn't put any gum in the box."
Maggie nodded. "The next clue was in the box too." She took the piece of paper out of her shorts pocket and held it up.
William's parents traded a confused look. "Are you sure there wasn't a white envelope in the box too?" William's father asked.
"We're sure," Henry said. "There was nothing inside except the clue, some tissue paper, and a few sticks of gum."
"What was in the envelope?" Luke asked William's parents.
"Your booty," William's father answered. "Seven movie tickets—one for each of you."
"Movie tickets?" Maggie said.
William's mother nodded. "Not just ordinary movie tickets, either," she said. "They were for the local premiere of Revenge of the Pirate's Ghost. "
The kids gasped. That was the title of the new pirate movie that was coming out next month.
" Revenge of the Pirate's Ghost ?" Nathan cried. "I'm dying to see that!"
"You know what this means, don't you?" Maggie said.
"What?" Luke asked.
"Someone stole our pirate booty." Maggie glanced at Henry and Cole. "This is a job for The Lemonade Detectives!"
"Thanks for lunch," Henry told William's parents a half hour later. "It was delicious."
"You're welcome, Henry." William's mother smiled. "And don't worry about the movie tickets that are missing. We'll investigate what happened to them."
"You should talk to Roger Redbeard first," Nathan said. "I bet he's the one who took them."
"Yeah!" Cole said. "He was hanging around when we found our hats, remember? Maybe he saw the clue then."
"I don't think so," Henry said. "He left before we opened the trunk."
William's father chuckled. "Roger Redbeard? I'm sure he didn't take your tickets."
William's mother nodded. "He has a pretty successful business running pirate tours for tourists."
But Maggie wasn't convinced. "He seemed a little weird to me."
William's mother patted her on the arm. "Just enjoy the rest of the treasure hunt, kids. We'll figure out what to do about those missing tickets."
The kids headed down to the beach. Maggie held out the next clue so they could all see it. It was a drawing of a boat with a pirate flag.
"It looks like our next booty is hidden on a boat," Henry said.
"Hey, William, maybe it's at the Sea Cove Marina where people keep their boats," Luke said.
William just shrugged. Henry had noticed that he still seemed kind of grumpy.
"We should check the marina." Anna looked at the drawing again. "But this drawing could also mean that our booty is at the Pirate Ship."
Nathan looked excited. "Pirate ship?"
"It's not a real ship," Luke told him. "Just a big rock on the northern part of the island."
Anna nodded. "People call it that because it looks like a ship." She pointed up the beach. "You can see the top of it from here."
"Maybe we should split up again," Henry suggested. "Cole and Maggie and I will walk to the Pirate Ship. You guys can walk to the bay and check out the marina."
"Good plan," Luke agreed. "Come on, guys!"
As soon as the others were out of sight, Henry looked at Cole and Maggie. "I had an ulterior motive for saying we should split up," he said.
"A what?" Maggie asked.
"An ulterior motive," Henry repeated as the three of them walked slowly along the beach. "It means a secret motive."
"Then why not just say secret motive?" Maggie asked.
"Never mind," Henry said. "I just meant that I wanted to get The Lemonade Detectives alone so we could talk about the mystery."
"William's parents think someone stumbled across those tickets and grabbed them," said Maggie.
"A crime of opportunity," Cole said.
"Right," Henry said. "But that doesn't really make sense. This is a private beach. There's hardly anybody out here."
"Except that weird Roger Redbeard," Maggie said.

Henry stepped over some rocks along the beach. He and his friends were getting closer to the Pirate Ship. "William's parents don't think Roger did it. But I think he should be on our suspect list anyway."
"Me too," Cole agreed. "Are there any other suspects?"
"What about Luke?" Maggie said. "He's crazy about pirates. And he and Nathan were talking about wanting to see that movie."
